The IA Cycle

Unit 8 • SL

~35 Lessons (Approx. 14 Teaching Weeks) • B

Unit Overview

The Internal Assessment (IA) focuses on the Iterative Cycle of software development. It moves beyond simple coding to encompass the full computational thinking process: identifying a human need, designing a robust solution, building complex logic, and critically evaluating the result against measurable success criteria.

What You'll Learn

  • Criterion A: Problem specification (measurable requirements) and Stakeholder identification (~300 words).
  • Criterion B: Planning, decomposition of the problem, and a chronology of steps (GANTT/Agile) (~150 words).
  • Criterion C: System overview (UML/Flowcharts), UI design, and a comprehensive testing strategy (~150 words).
  • Criterion D: Development (algorithmic complexity, implementation of data structures) and the 5-minute video demonstration (~1000 words).
  • Criterion E: Evaluation of success criteria and recommendations for future improvement (~400 words).
  • Appendices: Full source code and authentication documentation.

Key Terminology

Master these terms to succeed in this unit:

Solution (Doc + Video) Product (Software only) Stakeholder Success Criteria Measurability Decomposition GANTT Chart System Model Appendix Screencast Word Count (2 000 max)

Common Misconceptions

  • Documentation vs. Code: Students often mistakenly believe the IA is only about the code. The documentation determines the majority of the marks.
  • Innovation vs. Templates: Believing that using a pre-existing template (e.g., a simple web template) is acceptable. Innovation and modification must be explicitly documented.
  • Teacher Debugging: Expecting the teacher to write or debug the source code. Teachers must remain as advisors, not co-developers.

Big Ideas to Consider

  • Ethics of Data: What is the developer's responsibility regarding the confidentiality and security of original data collected from stakeholders?
  • Knowledge Transformation: Does the process of translating a human problem into a code-based solution lose essential nuances of the original context?
